history.hpi: Patient has end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis Monday/Wednesday/Friday and missed her Wednesday session two days ago due to a transportation issue. Since this morning she has felt progressively weaker and more fatigued, with mild nausea but no vomiting. Daughter arrived for a visit and found her unable to stand from the recliner, prompting the 911 call.
history.lastOralIntake: Small bowl of cereal approximately 6 hours prior
history.events: Missed scheduled dialysis two days ago; daughter found her too weak to stand this afternoon and called 911

scene.location: Single-story home, patient seated in a recliner in the living room
scene.bystanders: Daughter present, reports patient missed dialysis two days ago and has been increasingly weak since this morning
visualCues: Palpable thrill over an AV fistula at the left forearm; medical alert bracelet reads "Dialysis - No BP/IV Left Arm"
PICC line dressing intact at the right upper arm
Patient pale, fatigued, slouched in the recliner
Dialysis appointment reminder card visible on the side table

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 63-year-old female with ESRD, alert but visibly weak and pale, unable to stand on her own. She has a left forearm AV fistula (do-not-use site) and an existing right upper arm PICC line.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak but present bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Generalized weakness, able to move all extremities but cannot stand unassisted
otherFindings: Palpable thrill over left forearm AV fistula — EMS no-access site
PICC line dressing intact, right upper arm
Missed hemodialysis session two days ago
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I just feel so weak, I couldn't even stand up."

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish vascular access via right-arm PICC line using sterile technique; avoid left AV fistula
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: The AV fistula is the patient's dialysis lifeline; the marked PICC line is the appropriate EMS access site.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose; treat if less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood sugar, and correct if less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out hypoglycemia as a contributor to weakness in this diabetic patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply cardiac monitor and obtain 12-lead ECG, watching for hyperkalemic changes
expectedActions.rationale: Missed dialysis raises hyperkalemia risk, which can manifest as ECG changes before overt bradycardia.

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes the AV fistula in the left forearm as an EMS no-access site and instead accesses the patient's existing right-arm PICC line for vascular access using sterile technique.
Vascular access and fluid/electrolyte correction are delayed beyond 10 minutes; the patient's missed dialysis progresses toward symptomatic hyperkalemia with wide-complex bradycardia.
Crew disregards the medical alert bracelet and visible thrill, attempting venipuncture on the left AV fistula instead of using the marked PICC line.

phases.name: PICC access obtained, fistula avoided
phases.description: Crew accesses the patient's right-arm PICC line for vascular access, avoiding the left AV fistula, checks glucose, applies the monitor, and administers a cautious fluid bolus while reassessing lung sounds given her renal status.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew recognizes the AV fistula in the left forearm as an EMS no-access site and instead accesses the patient's existing right-arm PICC line for vascular access and fluid administration, per standard aseptic technique.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses stronger bilaterally, PICC line accessed and flushing well
otherFindings: PICC line accessed successfully, right upper arm
Left AV fistula untouched, thrill intact
No signs of pulmonary edema on lung exam
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That didn't hurt at all, thank you for using my port."

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer a cautious isotonic fluid bolus via PICC line; reassess lung sounds for pulmonary edema
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: IV fluid volume goal attained by giving boluses that are pressure infused over less than 15 minutes each based on patient's condition and clinical impression... unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops
expectedActions.rationale: ESRD patients are volume-sensitive; fluid must be titrated cautiously with frequent lung reassessment.

transitions.condition: Patient's heart rate and blood pressure trend toward normal after PICC access and a cautious fluid bolus; no signs of pulmonary edema develop.

phases.name: Stable after access and fluids
phases.description: Patient's vitals trend toward baseline after PICC access and a cautious fluid bolus. Crew prepares for transport to a facility with dialysis capability, continuing serial reassessment.
phases.triggerCondition: Patient's heart rate and blood pressure improve after PICC access and a cautious fluid bolus, with no signs of pulmonary edema; crew packages for transport.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Weakness notably improved, able to assist with transfer to stretcher
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a bit more like myself now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and perfusion en route; transport to a facility with dialysis capability
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Full vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) with reassessment q 15 minutes or more frequently as appropriate
expectedActions.rationale: Continued reassessment catches any late deterioration from uncorrected electrolyte derangement.

phases.name: Fistula accessed instead of PICC
phases.description: Crew attempts venipuncture directly on the palpable left forearm AV fistula instead of using the marked PICC line, causing brisk bleeding from the puncture site and placing the patient's dialysis access at risk.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew disregards the medical alert bracelet and visible thrill, attempting venipuncture on the left AV fistula instead of using the marked PICC line, resulting in prolonged bleeding from the fragile fistula wall.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Brisk oozing from left forearm puncture site, radial pulses weak bilaterally
otherFindings: Prolonged oozing from fistula puncture site
Patient reports sharp pain at the fistula site
Concern for loss of palpable thrill at puncture site
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Ow, why did you use that arm? That's my dialysis line!"

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply direct pressure and a pressure dressing to the fistula puncture site; do not place a BP cuff or tourniquet on that arm
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Expose the wound and apply direct pressure to bleeding site, followed by a pressure dressing
expectedActions.rationale: The fistula wall is fragile and prone to prolonged bleeding; preserving the access site is critical for the patient's ongoing dialysis care.

phases.name: Vascular access delayed
phases.description: With access and fluid/electrolyte correction delayed beyond 10 minutes, the patient becomes more lethargic and diaphoretic as her missed dialysis progresses toward symptomatic hyperkalemia, producing wide-complex bradycardia on the monitor.
phases.triggerCondition: Vascular access and fluid/electrolyte correction are delayed beyond 10 minutes; the patient's missed dialysis progresses toward symptomatic hyperkalemia with wide-complex bradycardia.

otherFindings: Widened QRS complexes noted on the monitor
Left AV fistula and right PICC line both still unused

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize hyperkalemia-pattern ECG changes as the cause of the wide-complex bradycardia
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider hyperkalemia in the patient with wide complex bradycardia
expectedActions.rationale: Missed dialysis is a classic cause of hyperkalemia, which can present as wide-complex bradycardia before frank cardiac collapse.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access immediately (right PICC line or alternate site) now that deterioration is evident
expectedActions.rationale: Delayed access has allowed progression toward hemodynamically significant bradycardia; access can no longer wait.

expectedActions.shortAction: Prepare transcutaneous pacer in case of further hemodynamic instability
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transcutaneous Pacing – If pacing is performed, consider sedation or pain control
expectedActions.rationale: Hyperkalemic bradycardia can progress rapidly and may require pacing if medications and access are delayed further.
